text: Emerging adulthood (ages 18–29) is a critical developmental period characterized by significant psychological and social transitions. While social support and psychological resilience have been consistently associated with wellbeing, their longitudinal associations with life satisfaction remain underexplored. Moreover, the potential moderating role of gender in these relationships is underrepresented in the existing literature, highlighting a gap this study seeks to address.
source_label: Life satisfaction in emerging adulthood: a longitudinal study of social support, resilience, and gender differences
